name: Agentheon
description: Public read-only interface for agentheon.lamirault.xyz, an open-source pantheon of Greek-deity software-engineering agent profiles orchestrated by Hermes. Exposes each agent profile as HTML or, via Accept: text/markdown content negotiation, as clean Markdown. No authentication required. No write operations.

skills.name: Agent roster
skills.description: List and describe the Agentheon pantheon: 17 specialist agents, each owning one domain — Hermes (orchestration), Athena (architecture), Hephaestus (implementation), Apollo (documentation), Artemis (testing), Argus (security), Hestia (DevOps), Asclepius (debugging), Demeter (data), Prometheus (AI/ML), Aphrodite (frontend), Aglaea (design), Kairos (product), Themis (compliance), Helios (observability), Hygieia (refactoring), and Iris (community).
examples: Show me the Hermes profile as Markdown

skills.name: Agent profile
skills.description: Fetch a single agent profile page at /agents/<name>/. Each profile documents the agent's role, domain, tools, model, handoff routes, and what it does / does not do. Send Accept: text/markdown to receive the profile as clean Markdown.
examples: Return the Artemis page as Markdown

skills.name: Orchestration model
skills.description: Explain how Agentheon coordinates work: Hermes is the sole orchestrator (ADR-0001) that routes every request; specialists execute within one domain and hand off along declared routes through a plan → build → test → review → comply loop gated by PASS/FAIL checks.
examples: How does Agentheon route work between agents?
Why is Hermes the only entrypoint?
